caption: Is Boaz a preview of Jesus? His costly rescue makes meaningful Christian typology. But Ruth describes family property and marriage—not a forecast of Christ’s redemption.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Boaz predict Jesus? Boaz acts as Ruth’s family redeemer. Christians see him as a picture of Jesus redeeming believers.
slides.body: Boaz acts as Ruth’s family redeemer. Christians see him as a picture of Jesus redeeming believers.
slides.heading: Did Boaz predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ruth 4:4-10: Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.
slides.body: Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.
slides.heading: Ruth 4:4-10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Eph 1:7, BSB: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace
slides.body: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Eph 1:7

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why the comparison works Boaz accepts a costly duty, rescues a vulnerable family and becomes an ancestor of David—and therefore of Jesus.
slides.body: Boaz accepts a costly duty, rescues a vulnerable family and becomes an ancestor of David—and therefore of Jesus.
slides.heading: Why the comparison works

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Ruth tells Boaz’s story His redemption concerns land, marriage and a family name. Ephesians never calls Jesus a kinsman or links him with Ruth.
slides.body: His redemption concerns land, marriage and a family name. Ephesians never calls Jesus a kinsman or links him with Ruth.
slides.heading: But Ruth tells Boaz’s story

title: Boaz the kinsman-redeemer
